column1: fraudulent§A fraudulent signature is usually too careful.§**伪造**的签名通常写得太工整。
frisky§The wind was frisky and the flags never settled.§风很**调皮**，旗子一直不肯安分。
frivolity§Frivolity at the right moment saved a very tense meeting.§适时的一点**轻松**救了一场极其紧张的会议。
frivolous§The suit was dismissed as frivolous and refiled twice.§这起诉讼被以**无理由**驳回，又两次重新提起。
frolicsome§A frolicsome puppy makes a poor companion in a library.§**活蹦乱跳**的小狗不适合在图书馆里作伴。
frugal§Frugal with paper, he wrote on both sides of everything.§他用纸**节俭**，什么都两面写。
frustration§Frustration teaches you where the design is wrong.§**挫败感**告诉你设计错在哪里。
fulsome§Fulsome apologies suggest the offense was worse than admitted.§**过度的**道歉暗示冒犯比承认的更严重。
funerary§Funerary inscriptions are the best source for ordinary names.§**墓志铭**是了解普通人姓名的最佳来源。
furious§The pace was furious for an hour and then collapsed.§节奏**猛烈**了一小时，随后就垮了。
futile§It is futile to argue with a timetable.§跟时刻表争论是**徒劳**的。
futility§There is a certain comfort in accepting the futility of the task.§承认这项任务的**徒劳**，反而有一种安慰。
gaffe§The gaffe was minor and the coverage was not.§这次**失言**很小，报道却不小。
gaiety§Forced gaiety is harder to watch than plain gloom.§强装的**欢乐**比坦率的阴郁更难看。
gall§The gall bladder was the reason for the whole hospital stay.§**胆囊**是这次住院的全部原因。
gallantry§Gallantry in the record often means somebody died.§记录中的“**英勇**”往往意味着有人牺牲。
galvanize§A closure notice galvanized a street that had never organized.§一张关闭通知**发动**了一条从未组织起来的街道。
garner§The exhibition garnered attention it could not accommodate.§这个展览**获得**了它容纳不下的关注。
garnish§Wages were garnished until the debt was cleared.§工资被**扣发**，直到债务还清。
gaudy§The gaudy jacket sold a book the plain one would not have.§**花哨的**护封卖出了一本朴素封面卖不动的书。
generalize§Do not generalize from the only case you happen to know.§不要从你恰好知道的唯一一个例子作**推广**。
generic§Generic advice is advice nobody can act on.§**一般**化的建议是谁也无法据以行动的建议。
generosity§Generosity with credit costs nothing and buys everything.§在归功上**慷慨**不花分文，却能换来一切。
genial§A genial refusal is still worth practising.§**和蔼的**拒绝同样值得练习。
gentleness§Gentleness with materials is what separates repair from damage.§对材料的**轻柔**，是修复与损坏的分界。
geology§Geology decides where a town can grow and where it cannot.§**地质**决定一座城镇能往哪里发展，不能往哪里发展。
germinate§The idea germinated in a footnote and grew into a book.§这个想法在一条脚注里**萌芽**，长成了一本书。
gibe§Gibes from the gallery did not shorten the speech.§看台上的**嘲讽**并没有让演讲变短。
glorify§Do not glorify a process that nearly killed everyone involved.§不要**美化**一个几乎害死所有参与者的过程。
gluttonous§A gluttonous first draft can be cut to a lean second.§**臃肿**的初稿可以删成精瘦的二稿。
governmental§Governmental records survive; private ones usually do not.§**政府**记录得以留存，私人记录通常不会。
graceless§A graceless apology is worse than a graceful silence.§**没有风度**的道歉比有风度的沉默更糟。
gracious§Gracious in defeat is a harder skill than gracious in victory.§输时**有风度**比赢时有风度更难。
grandiose§The grandiose name hides a very small society.§这个**宏大的**名称背后是一个极小的社团。
grate§Snow fell through the grate and melted on the stones.§雪从**炉栅**落下，在石头上化开。
gratify§It gratifies nobody to be right about a disaster.§在灾难上说对了，谁也不会因此**高兴**。
gratuitous§The violence is gratuitous and the film loses by it.§其中的暴力**毫无必要**，影片因此逊色。
grimy§A grimy label turned out to hold the only date.§一张**脏兮兮**的标签上有着唯一的日期。
groundbreaking§Groundbreaking work is usually recognized as such much later.§**开创性**的工作通常很久以后才被认定。
gruff§A gruff greeting from him counted as warmth.§他一句**粗声粗气**的招呼，就算是热情了。
guesswork§Replace guesswork with a measurement whenever you can.§能测量的时候就别**靠猜**。
guileless§A guileless question can be the sharpest one in the room.§一个**天真**的问题可能是全场最尖锐的。
gullible§The market punishes the gullible and rewards the patient.§市场惩罚**轻信者**，奖赏耐心者。
hackneyed§Avoid the hackneyed opening and the reader stays.§避开**陈腐**的开头，读者就留下来了。
hallmark§The hallmark on the silver dates it to within a year.§银器上的**纯度印记**把年代精确到一年之内。
hamper§A picnic hamper from 1930 was found under the stairs.§楼梯下发现了一只一九三〇年的**野餐篮**。
haphazard§A haphazard sample tells you about the sampler.§**随意**抽取的样本说明的是取样的人。
hapless§The hapless timing meant nobody saw the announcement.§**倒霉的**时机让谁也没看见那则公告。
harangue§She listened to the harangue and answered one sentence of it.§她听完那通**训斥**，只回应了其中一句。
harass§Do not harass a witness who has already agreed to help.§不要**骚扰**一位已经同意帮忙的证人。
harbinger§The first swift is a harbinger nobody in the village misses.§第一只雨燕是村里没人会错过的**预兆**。
harmonic§Harmonic distortion was audible only on the loudest passages.§只有在最响的段落才听得出**谐波**失真。
harmonious§A harmonious committee usually means nobody is checking.§一个**和睦的**委员会通常意味着没人在核查。
harmonize§The two accounts refuse to harmonize on one date.§这两份记述在一个日期上无论如何都**对不上**。
harshly§The winter treated the roof harshly and the walls kindly.§这个冬天对屋顶很**苛刻**，对墙壁却很宽厚。
hasten§I hasten to add that the figure is provisional.§我要**赶紧**补充一句，这个数字是暂定的。
haughty§Haughty in print, he was diffident in person.§他落笔**傲慢**，见面却腼腆。
hazardous§Hazardous waste must be logged before it leaves the building.§**危险**废物在离开大楼前必须登记。
hedonistic§A hedonistic reading of the poem misses its unease.§**享乐主义**的解读会错过这首诗的不安。
heinous§The word heinous is now used for things that are merely rude.§“**可憎**”这个词如今被用来形容仅仅是无礼的事。
hesitant§A hesitant witness is not necessarily a dishonest one.§**犹豫**的证人未必是不诚实的。
hesitation§There was no hesitation in the signature at all.§那个签名毫无**迟疑**。
heterogeneity§Heterogeneity is the finding, not a flaw in the method.§**异质**性本身就是发现，而不是方法的缺陷。
hilarity§Hilarity in the back row derailed the rest of the class.§后排的**哄笑**打乱了这堂课的其余部分。
hindsight§Hindsight makes every decision look either obvious or stupid.§**事后之明**让每个决定看起来要么显而易见，要么愚蠢。
historian§A local historian knew the answer and nobody had asked her.§一位本地**史家**知道答案，却没人问过她。
histrionic§Cut the histrionic passages and a good short film remains.§删掉那些**戏剧化**的段落，剩下的是一部好的短片。
